beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:epic, restrained]Around {410|four ten} CE, the Roman Empire leaves ^Britain. [act:lower, simple]The lights go ^out. [act:mythic, building]And somewhere in the ^dark, about a century later, a war-leader wins a famous ^battle.
[d:tension][act:intrigued, pulling us in][tune:rise]Was his name ^Arthur? [act:warm, curious]The ^King Arthur of the legends?

[d:calm][act:sober, painting the loss]Britain after {410|four ten}: with Rome gone, ^coins, pottery and ^towns ^disappear. [p:0.93][act:explaining, simple]Almost nobody is ^writing. [act:a hint of wonder]That's why it's called a ^dark age: not because life stopped, but because the ^light we see it by goes out. [go:0|0][act:a hopeful turn, brighter]But in the ^west, at places like Tintagel, in the south-west, lords still imported pottery and glass from the ^Mediterranean.

[d:build][act:introducing a witness, keen]One writer lived through it: Gildas, writing around {540|five forty}, within living ^memory of the battle. [act:storytelling, vivid]He describes a great ^victory of the Britons over the Saxons, newcomers from across the North Sea, at a place called Mount ^Badon.
[d:build][sfx:hit][act:plain, a set-up]He names a ^hero: a leader called Ambrosius. [gap:0.4][act:quiet, pointed][tune:fall]Not ^Arthur.

[d:build][act:the problem, measured]The ^first text to name Arthur as that war-leader comes about three ^hundred years later, around {829|eight twenty-nine}, in a book called the History of the Britons. [gap:0.4][p:0.9][act:the everyday picture, clear]Three hundred years is about ^ten generations: imagine a story passed from grandparent to grandchild ten times before anyone writes it ^down. [act:explaining, the method]That's why historians give the most weight to the ^closest witness.

[d:build][go:2|0][act:light, a touch of wonder]And the ^shining King Arthur, with his court, arrives around {1136|eleven thirty-six}, more than six centuries after Badon, in a book by the writer ^Geoffrey of Monmouth.

[d:reveal][act:the turn, fair]Still: ^someone won Badon, and Gildas names almost ^nobody. [act:fair, opening it up]So, the ^candidates. [sfx:shimmer][act:laying out candidates][tune:level]^Riothamus, a British king who fought in ^Gaul, roughly today's France, around {470|four seventy}. [act:the second, curious][tune:level]A Roman officer in Britain called ^Artorius, a name much like Arthur's. [act:the third, softer][tune:fall]Or a hero of ^myth, given a ^history.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm][tune:rise]A ^real Arthur? [act:the verdict, level-headed][tune:fall]^*Open question*. [act:confident, plain]The ^battle was real: our one witness records@verb it. [act:honest, a gentle limit]The ^name can't be pinned on ^anyone.

[d:tension][p:0.93][act:the open door, sincere]Only a new ^text or inscription from the time, naming him, could change that. [act:quiet, sure][tune:fall]^Someone won Badon. [act:the last word, gentle, open][tune:fall]Whether his name was ^Arthur, the evidence may ^never say.
